title: Nice idea, but expensive for what you actually get
text:
Sure, it's convenient, but I just expected something a bit more than what was in the box.

Ingredients - I thought the box would have unusual or non- staple items. Nope. The most unusual for November was cranberries. Everything else was just pretty normal stuff. Now, if you want to re-create the box, i can see where you might just want staple items. I just thought for the price, there'd be something unique about the ingredients.

Packaging -- The packaging was inviting with well marked items and a tissue wrapper that made it into an experience to unwrap and explore. My one recommendation: it'd be nice to know the amount of each ingredient, in case you want to make more.

November bake -- it really was just a sweet sticky mess. I split the dough into 2; preserving the second batch to see how the first turned out. The needed much more flour to release from the pan, which was really a pain if you wait the 10 minutes to cool on the cooking sheet. The second batch I put in well sprayed muffin tins and they hung together better and was much easier clean (I didn't let the Rugelach cool -- I immediately removed from the pan. Much easier cleaning.

Bottom line: it's restaurant prices, but you do all the clean up yourself! I understand there's proprietary recipe and decorative packaging to give you the experience itself. It's just a bit too expensive.
